sources.title: FACT: Failure-Aware Causal Training for World-Action Models

sectionsRead: Title, abstract and contribution note (p. 1): arXiv:2608.10232v1, 10 August 2026
Appendix A: Training and Inference Algorithms (p. 14)
Appendix C: Real-World Setup and Task Prompts (pp. 15–16)
Appendices D–H: simulation details, latency, prediction metrics and value diagnostics (pp. 17–19)
omissions: Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; inspect the retained PDF for figures and equation/table layout.
The inspected title, five authors and affiliation match the catalog. This report concerns the supplied v1 dated 10 August 2026; no different revision or edition was supplied or compared.
Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; the retained PDF was therefore visually inspected for figures and equation/table layout.
Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.

synopsis: FACT learns actions and their consequences in one video transformer. Successful demonstrations supervise all outputs; failed rollouts supervise future video and task progress while their action-imitation loss is disabled. Action-only deployment skips future prediction, with optional action-conditioned scoring offering additional gains at extra computation.

problem.text: A model trained only on successful demonstrations can imagine success even under a bad action. FACT asks how failed rollouts can teach accurate consequences without teaching the policy to imitate those actions.

contributions.text: A clean teacher-forced action slot and attention mask separate action generation from consequence prediction inside a shared transformer.
Failure-aware video and progress supervision improves policy success and prediction of failed outcomes in the reported settings.

inputs: Language instruction; main and two wrist RGB views; robot proprioception.
During training, recorded action chunks, observed future frames, episode outcome and failure-onset annotations.
outputs: An action chunk; optionally, its predicted task-progress value and future video.

steps.name: Encode the robot context
steps.detail: The observation combines three camera views and proprioception. Camera streams are packed into one video canvas, with per-view VAE latents precomputed; task prompts provide T5 embeddings for text cross-attention.

steps.name: Separate noisy actions from clean action conditions
steps.detail: Tokens are ordered P, A, G, V, I: observation prefix, noisy predicted action, clean recorded action, value and future video. A cannot attend to G; V and I attend to G rather than noisy A. This prevents the policy from seeing its clean target.

steps.name: Share consequence learning with the policy
steps.detail: One causal video diffusion transformer processes the modalities, with an action adapter after each block's feed-forward network on robot tokens. World losses can update shared parameters used for action generation; masking action loss does not freeze the policy backbone.

training.text: Initialize from WAN2.2-5B and use AdamW: learning rates are 2×10⁻⁴ for the action FFN and 2×10⁻⁵ for the backbone. Action/value/video loss weights are 20/1/1; H=48 and the failure penalty is 1. Video targets use offsets [0,H/4,H/2,3H/4,H].

Flow matching interpolates clean modality tokens with Gaussian noise and learns the noise-minus-clean velocity by squared error. Algorithm 2 first trains on successes, collects failed policy rollouts, then continues mixed training. Failed windows retain video/value losses and lose action imitation.

inference.text: Stage 1 denoises actions from observation and state, normally for 20 flow-Euler steps, and can return immediately. Stage 2 conditions on the clean sampled action to predict value and optionally video. Candidate scoring ranks predicted consequences before executing the selected action; it does not require physically trying every candidate.
Optional real-world evaluation samples four candidates. The same model scores them; no separate critic is trained. The source reports prefix key-value caching for action-only inference.

equations.explanation: Equation (6): the recorded action chunk spans horizon H; p is normalized progress, instantiated as t/T for episode length T. The indicator records failure by the chunk endpoint, and the penalty lowers that target. With penalty 1, an endpoint marked failed has target zero; this is a deduction from the clipped formula.
Equations (8)–(9): successful data D_s supervise action a, value v and video I losses; failed data D_f supervise only value and video. The w terms weight those modality losses.

results.setting: Five tasks; 20 trials per task/method. Cube tasks use 200 success demonstrations and about 30 failures each; remaining tasks use 50 demonstrations.
results.value: Failure-trained FACT: 89; with optional four-candidate scoring: 92.
results.interpretation: Failure training adds 7 percentage points under single-sample control; optional scoring adds 3 more. Baselines share success fine-tuning data, but pretraining and failure supervision differ.

results.task: Unseen real-world object and instruction variants
results.setting: Held-out Stack Cubes, Pick Cubes and Stack Bowls variants change colors, shapes and instructions; 20 trials per cell.
results.interpretation: Reported rounded averages improve, but FACT remains below π₀.₅ on these variants.

results.setting: 50 tasks; 2,500 clean and 25,000 randomized training demonstrations plus about 1,300 failures; 100 evaluation trials per task per split.
results.interpretation: Video and failure co-training each improve the average, while Motus retains a small aggregate lead.

results.setting: Same five-task real-world benchmark. The causal-mask ablation uses success-only data and removes G while jointly denoising outputs.
results.value: Without causal mask: 77; with failed-action imitation: 63; without video: 58.
results.comparison: Success-only FACT: 82; failure-trained FACT with masked action loss: 89; success-only scoring: 79.
results.interpretation: Results support clean action conditioning and selective failure supervision. The mask ablation changes conditioning as well as attention; it is not an isolated one-edge intervention.

results.setting: 512 windows, evenly split between successful demonstrations and failed rollouts; both checkpoints use 20 denoising steps.
results.interpretation: The gain concentrates on failed futures. Image similarity supports consequence prediction, not a robot-success or calibration guarantee.

results.setting: Measured on an RTX PRO 6000; failure-trained FACT uses its action-only path.
results.interpretation: FACT is faster than these WAM comparators but slower than the listed action policies. This measurement excludes optional candidate scoring.

results.task: Failure-data scaling on three RoboTwin clean tasks
results.setting: Handover Block, Open Microwave and Put Bottles Dustbin; use 0%, 50% or 100% of available failures. At 100%, failures comprise about 45% of training data.
results.value: 32.7 to 57.3 from zero to all available failures.
results.comparison: Figure 6 reports a monotonic average across the three fractions.
results.interpretation: This restricted experiment supports additional failure supervision; individual task bars are not uniformly monotonic.

limitations.text: Broader robot/human data and improved progress estimators remain future work. Best-of-N adds a scoring pass; action-only control avoids that cost.

Only 20 real-world trials per cell are reported, without confidence intervals. Section 4.2 assigns N=4 to optional rows and calls other variants single-sample, leaving the separate 'Ours + scoring' ablation's candidate count ambiguous.

Progress targets use episode time and annotated failure onset rather than calibrated success probabilities. Appendix H explicitly leaves diagnostic predictions unclipped, explaining negative heat-map scores despite bounded targets. Figure 7 falls from four to eight candidates, although adjacent prose describes a smaller gain.

reproduction.text: Recreate the two YAM arms, D435 main camera, two D405 wrist cameras, GELLO collection, multi-view preprocessing and exact prompts. The PDF specifies learning rates and losses but omits batch size, training duration, training accelerator count and software versions.

Failure-onset annotation needs resolution: Section 3.3 assumes annotations, while Algorithm 2 says 'when available' without a fallback. Proposed checks should control data, compute and candidate pools when testing action-loss masking and value-based selection.

reasoning.text: Shared transformer blocks and robot-token adapters support One Model. The action-first, action-conditioned world branch supports Other mechanisms / Outside quadrants rather than inverse dynamics or simultaneous action/future denoising at deployment. Joint video-action training and policy continuation are present; reinforcement-learning updates are only a future direction, not a demonstrated component of the broad post-training/WM-RL label.

discussionQuestions: How sensitive is ranking to episode-length normalization and uncertain failure-onset labels?
Does failure supervision improve shared action representations when training compute and candidate pools are held fixed?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title block, author footnote and arXiv margin
evidence.detail: Title and all five authors match; UC San Diego affiliation; Peng and Liang contributed equally; v1 is dated 10 August 2026.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–2, abstract and Section 1
evidence.detail: Motivates learning failed consequences without imitating failed actions; introduces optional scoring.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Sections 3.1–3.2, Equations (1)–(4)
evidence.detail: Defines instruction, multiview observation, proprioception, action horizon, future observations and normalized progress.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Figures 2–3, Equation (5), Section 3.2
evidence.detail: Shared transformer with robot-token adapters; training V/I attend G, not A; A cannot see G. Inference diagram labels A but annotates transfer of the denoised action to G.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.3, Equation (6) and implementation details
evidence.detail: Progress uses t/T, failure-onset indicator and clipped penalty; experimental failure penalty equals 1.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.3, Equations (7)–(9) and implementation details
evidence.detail: Flow matching, success/failure losses, WAN2.2-5B initialization, AdamW, learning rates, loss weights, 48-step chunks and future offsets are specified.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, two-stage inference, optional scoring and Equation (10)
evidence.detail: Action denoising can run alone; optional world pass conditions on each clean candidate and selects maximal progress; prefix caching and 20 default steps are reported.

evidence.location: PDF p. 14, Appendix A, Algorithms 1–3
evidence.detail: Success training precedes failed-rollout collection and co-training; failure actions are masked; onset is annotated when available; candidate scoring precedes selected action return.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 4.2; p. 15, Appendix B
evidence.detail: Five seen and three unseen variants; demonstration/failure counts; 20 trials per cell; optional rows use four candidates while the prose calls other variants single-sample.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Tables 2–3, FACT and external-baseline rows, Avg. columns
evidence.detail: Seen averages are 82/89/92 for FACT variants and 64/88 for Motus/π₀.₅; unseen averages are 67/77/82 and 62/85.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 4.1 and Table 1, Clean/Rand./Average columns
evidence.detail: About 1.3K failures are added; FACT averages are 81.8 without video, 85.6 success-only and 87.5 with failures; Motus is 87.8.

evidence.location: PDF p. 17, Appendix D; p. 18, Table 6 and caption
evidence.detail: Training totals are 2,500 clean and 25,000 randomized demonstrations across 50 tasks; evaluation uses 100 trials per task/split. Per-task results include both gains and regressions.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 2 ablation rows and Section 4.3 policy-performance paragraph
evidence.detail: Seen averages: scoring alone 79, no causal mask 77, failed-action loss 63, no video 58. The causal-mask variant removes clean G and jointly denoises outputs without failure data.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 4; p. 17, Appendix F; p. 19, Table 8, all rows and metric columns
evidence.detail: 512 held-out windows split equally by outcome, 20 steps. Failure PSNR/SSIM rise 19.51/0.7461 to 25.92/0.8290; success metrics remain nearly unchanged.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Figure 5 and caption
evidence.detail: Under the same bad-action condition, the success-only prediction shows a successful grasp in the dotted box, whereas failure-trained prediction resembles the observed failed outcome.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, failure-data scaling paragraph and Figure 6
evidence.detail: Three-task average rises 32.7 to 57.3 across failure fractions; the full failure set is about 45% of training data. Put Bottles Dustbin declines at the intermediate fraction.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, value-guided candidate scoring paragraph and Figure 7
evidence.detail: Same-checkpoint candidate sweep measures relative completion and latency. The plotted completion peaks at four then falls at eight, despite prose describing smaller gains for larger sets.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Figure 8; p. 17, Appendices G–H and Figure 12; p. 19, Figure 13
evidence.detail: Example values fall on missed grasps and recover; a 3×3 placement diagnostic scores the successful center highest. Appendix H explicitly states predictions are unclipped.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Sections 5–6
evidence.detail: Broader data and improved progress estimators are future work; scoring costs an extra pass; online corrections and reinforcement learning are proposed extensions.

evidence.location: PDF p. 15, Appendix C; p. 16, Figure 11
evidence.detail: Two YAM arms, D435 main camera, two D405 wrist cameras and GELLO; packed multiview canvas and precomputed VAE latents; baselines share success fine-tuning demonstrations.

evidence.location: PDF p. 16, Table 5 and caption
evidence.detail: Lists the five real-world task prompts and states that T5 embeddings feed cross-attention.

evidence.location: PDF p. 17, Appendix E; p. 19, Table 7, model/inference-time column
evidence.detail: RTX PRO 6000 measurements: FACT with failures 380 ms, Motus 1220, Cosmos 620, π₀.₅ 47, π₀ 45; Appendix E identifies FACT's action-only deployment.
